overview: Egypt is a country in the north-east corner of Africa, with the Sinai Peninsula reaching into Asia. Its capital, Cairo, is one of the largest cities in Africa and the Middle East. Ancient Egypt was one of the world's first great civilisations, and its pyramids at Giza are among the most famous monuments on Earth. The Suez Canal, which links the Mediterranean and Red seas, runs through Egypt.

geography.text: Almost all of Egypt is desert, and nearly everyone lives along the Nile, the longest river in Africa, or in its delta on the Mediterranean. The Western Desert has oases and the Qattara Depression, which lies below sea level, while the Eastern Desert and Sinai are mountainous. Lake Nasser, behind the Aswan High Dam, is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world.

history.text: Ancient Egypt was one of the world's first great civilisations. Its pharaohs built the pyramids of Giza around 4,500 years ago. Egypt was later ruled by Greeks, Romans, Arabs, Ottomans and the British. It became independent in 1922, and a revolution in 1952 ended the monarchy. Egypt fought several wars with Israel before signing a peace treaty in 1979.

events.title: Unification
events.text: Upper and Lower Egypt are united.

events.title: Great Pyramid
events.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza is completed.

events.title: Roman rule
events.text: Cleopatra dies and Egypt becomes part of Rome.

events.title: Suez Canal
events.text: The canal linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea opens.

events.title: Peace with Israel
events.text: Egypt and Israel sign a peace treaty.

government.text: Egypt is a presidential republic in which the President holds strong powers. Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, a former army chief, took power in 2013 after the military removed the elected president, Mohamed Morsi. Opposition and protests are tightly restricted.

economy.text: Egypt's economy relies on tourism, money sent home by Egyptians abroad, natural gas, and tolls from the Suez Canal, through which about a tenth of world trade normally passes. Farming along the Nile is also important.

culture.text: Ancient Egypt gave the world the pyramids, hieroglyphs and the Sphinx. Most of Egypt's 100-plus million people live along the Nile. Cairo is the largest city in the Arab world, and Egyptian films and music are watched across it. The Grand Egyptian Museum opened beside the pyramids in 2025.

items.title: Pyramids of Giza
items.text: The only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.

items.title: Koshari
items.text: Rice, lentils and pasta, a national dish.

sport.text: Football is Egypt's passion, and it has won the Africa Cup of Nations a record seven times. Mohamed Salah is one of the best players in the world. Egypt also dominates squash.

items.title: Mohamed Salah
items.text: Premier League and Champions League winner with Liverpool.

items.title: Squash
items.text: Egyptians have often held the top world rankings.
